assets/binary-formats.title: Asset Binary Formats
assets/binary-formats.description: TurtleStudio edits assets as JSON on disk. When exporting to the SD package (build/), pixel data is baked into compact binary files.

assets/sprite-spec.title: Sprite Spec
assets/sprite-spec.description: Sprites in TurtleStudio are JSON assets stored in objects/Sprites/.json. They define pixel art with optional multiple frames, a palette reference, an anchor origin, and a collision shape when attached to an object.

cartridge/turtlecart-format.title: .turtlecart Format
cartridge/turtlecart-format.description: A .turtlecart file is a plain-text container with an ordered set of sections. It's designed for simplicity: readable on any text editor, easy to parse on the ESP32.

gui/gui-layers.title: GUI Layers
gui/gui-layers.description: GUI layers are stackable overlays defined in the cart bundle and shown/hidden at runtime from Lua. They handle menus, dialogues, inventory screens, title cards, game-over screens, and non-modal popups — any transient UI that doesn't fit in the permanent HUD strip.

gui/hud-border.title: HUD Border
gui/hud-border.description: The HUD border reserves fixed pixel strips along the framebuffer edges for permanent on-screen UI — score, lives, minimap, timer — by shrinking the camera's playfield. This is method 1 of GUI transient overlays for menus, pause screens, and dialogues.

intro.title: Introduction
intro.description: TurtleReader is a fantasy console targeting the ESP32-S3 microcontroller. Games are distributed as .turtlecart cartridges stored on a microSD card. Game logic runs on an embedded Lua 5.4 VM.

lua/animation.title: Animation
lua/animation.description: Sprite animation is controlled from Lua via the animations list defined in the object's JSON. C++ advances frames automatically after _update(dt) runs.

lua/entry-vm.title: ENTRY VM
lua/entry-vm.description: The ENTRY script is declared in the ENTRY scripts/global.lua). The firmware executes it once during setup(), before the scene runtime starts.

lua/object-scripts.title: Object Scripts
lua/object-scripts.description: Object scripts provide per-instance game logic: reading input, moving, and changing animations. Sprite drawing and the frame loop stay in C++ (turtle_scene); Lua decides behavior and position.

lua/overview.title: Lua API Overview
lua/overview.description: TurtleReader runs two independent Lua VMs that do not share state. Each has a distinct lifecycle and API surface.

lua/physics.title: Physics
lua/physics.description: Movement and collision for actors in scene. Inspired by Godot's moveandcollide — per-axis, no slope sliding.

scene/scene-format.title: Scene Format
scene/scene-format.description: A scene defines the visual space where a game takes place0; no field in any version is required.

turtlestudio/guide.title: TurtleStudio Guide
turtlestudio/guide.description: TurtleStudio is the Python authoring tool for TurtleReader projects. It ships a CLI and a Dear PyGui GUI editor.
